 This Mfa Filed U/S 173(1) Of Mv Act Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 15.5.2012 Passed In Mvc
No.573/2007 On The File Of The Principal Senior Civil
Judge(Sr.Dn) & Cjm, Mact, Mandya, Dismissing The
Claim Petition For Compensation.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Dismissal, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Aggrieved by the dismissal of M.V.C.No.573/2007 dated 15th May of 2012 the claimant is before this Court.
The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.3,25,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident.

2. The case of the claimant is that, on 14.05.2007 at about 10.00 a.m., when he was standing on the road side at Padarahally on Magadi-Ramanagara road, at that time one Tipper lorry driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner came from Magadi side and dashed against the Motor Cycle and then dashed against the petitioners, as a result of this the claimant sustained multiple injuries thereafter he was shifted to Divisional NC: 2023:KHC:33868 hospital, Ramanagara and then to Nimhans and on 15.05.2007 again he admitted to Mandya District Hospital.
He has sustained lacerated injury over head, over occipital region, and on other parts of the body.
The petitioner was treated as inpatient in Mandya District Hospital from 15.05.2007 to 17.05.2007.
3. It is a case of the insurance company that the vehicle itself is not involved in the accident and even as per the medical records he has sustained injuries as it is a fall from the bike.

The Court below has analyzed the evidence of PW-1 where he has stated in the cross- examination that the police have not enquired him with regard to the accident, he do not remember the registration number of Motor Cycle or lorry, he do not know who is driving the scooter or pillion was one who is his cousin and other contents were denied by PW-1.
Even in the accident registration extract it is mentioned that history of the road preferred accident on 14.5.2007 at about 08:40 a.m. caused out of fall from two wheeler.

The NC: 2023:KHC:33868 Court also observes that, in the petition it is stated that he had suffered injuries on 14.05.2007 at about 10:00 a.m., when he was hit by the Tipper Lorry while he was standing on the side of the road.
4. Ex.R3 is accident register extract produced with the consent of the claimant.
As per the same he sustained injuries due to fall from two wheeler after colluding with the lorry and he took treatment in the hospital at about 10:00 a.m.

As per the MVI report there is no damage to the tipper lorry and the motor vehicle is damaged and as per the wound certificate Ex.P4 issued by Ramanagara Government hospital that the accident took place at 08:45 a.m. on 14.05.2007 and the injured was examined by the doctor on the same day at about 10:00 a.m.

Ex.P7 is the copy of the charge sheet Sathisha vs Chandrashekar B H on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133771594/
2 which shows that injured has been cited as CW.3 by the police but the name mentioned therein though Sathish, his age about 26 years, S/o one Shambu and resident of Chamundipur village,
Kootgal hobli, Ramanagara Taluk who is nothing to do with NC: 2023:KHC:33868 the claimant herein.

Even as per Ex.P9 the petitioner was admitted in emergency ward of Nimhans on 15.05.2007 where he was admitted in Mandya Government hospital on 14.05.2007 and he was discharged on 19.05.2007 and there was no record of referring the patient to Nimhans by the Mandya Government hospital and the claimant could not have got examined any doctor of Nimhans.

The Court observed that the document Ex.P9 found to be a fabricated one Ex.P10 is another copy of emergency case record of Nimhans in which the date and time of the injury is given by the informant as 14.05.2007 at 08:45 a.m., and the petitioner discharged on the same day about 11:50 p.m., which runs contrary to the contents of Ex.P9 of the same hospital.

Ex.P11 is an inpatient record of the Government hospital Mandya in which Satish, the injured is shown as the son of one Motegowda resident of Varadahalli village, Maddur Taluk which do not tally with the claimant's father's name and his residence as he given in the cause title of the petition.

Considering this evidence, the Court has come to the conclusion that, the documents produced by the claimant the FIR, charge sheet and the medical documents run contrary to each other and even there is a discrepancy with regard to the name of the father of the claimant and dismissed the claim petition.
6. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that the FIR was registered basing on a complaint of the third party who is no where related to the claimants.
He submits that there are minor discrepancies in the medical evidence as well as the FIR, charge sheet.
He submits that, mere discrepancies cannot be a ground to dismiss the claim petition.
It is submitted that the Court below ought to have examine the case on the touch stone of preponderance of probability but not beyond reasonable doubt.
He has relied on the order of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Vimala devi and other V/s.
Himachand road transport corporation and others reported in1 and 2009-13 SCC 530 NC: 2023:KHC:33868 another order passed by this Court in MFA.No.9553/2007 c/w MFA.No.9197/2007 dated 30.06.2010.

Relying on these two judgments, the learned counsel submits that these discrepancies will not go to the root of the matter and the Court below considering the charge sheet and the FIR ought to have considered the claim petition filed by the claimant.

7. On the other hand learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that, when application is filed under Section 166 of the Act, the burden lies on the claimant to prove that there was an accident and the accident had taken place because of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
He submits that in this case there was no such proof.
In view of the discrepancies and contradictions, the Court below had rightly dismissed the petition.
8. This Court having heard the learned counsel on either side perused the entire material on record.
NC: 2023:KHC:33868 Sathisha vs Chandrashekar B H on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133771594/
3 9. There are severe discrepancies in this case.
According to the claimant, he was admitted in Nimhans hospital and thereafter he discharged and admitted to the other hospital.

The evidence on record clearly shows that he was admitted in Mandya Government hospital on 14.05.2007 at about 10:00 am and he was discharged on 19.05.2007 whereas Ex.P10 is the emergency case record of Nimhans in which the date and time of the injury is given by the informant at 08:45 a.m., on 14.05.2007 and he was discharged on the same day at 11:50 a.m.
These two documents create any doubt in the mind of the court about the accident and the admission of the claimant in the hospital.
10. It is the submission of the learned counsel that these discrepancies are not relevant as proof.
These cases are only on preponderance of probability.

This court is not able to appreciate the said contention as the discrepancies that are on record goes to the root of the matter about the accident as well as the treatment that is taken by the NC: 2023:KHC:33868 claimant coupled with other documents.
There is also discrepancy in the father's name of the claimant and other details.
11. In the light of these facts and circumstances, the Court below was right in dismissing the petition and this Court finds no reason to interfere.
Accordingly, appeal stands dismissed.

SD/-
